html:
The Mausoleum of Sultan Sanjar is a domed tomb at Merv in Turkmenistan, built for Ahmad Sanjar, the last great sultan of the Seljuk Empire, who died in 1157.

Sanjar ruled from Merv for some sixty years. He was captured by the Oghuz Turks in 1153 and held for three years, and the empire broke up soon after his death. His tomb is a brick cube with a double dome, once covered in blue tiles, and a gallery around the drum. Its builder signed his name inside.

It was among the largest domed buildings of its time. It survived the Mongol sack of 1221 when most of the city fell, and its double dome was taken up in later Persian building.
sum: The Mausoleum of Sultan Sanjar is a domed tomb at Merv in Turkmenistan, built for Ahmad Sanjar, the last great sultan of the Seljuk Empire, who died in 1157.
